sources.cite: Emerson, Rosemount 3051 Pressure Transmitter with HART Protocol, reference manual 00809-0100-4007 rev. BA (2017): §3.5 integral manifolds, §4.3 LCD display, §6.4 disassembly and §6.5 reassembly procedures, appendix A spare parts (the LCD display cover comes with its window)

manifold.name: Valve manifold
manifold.does: Bolted under the process flange: its valves isolate the transmitter from the process and equalise its two sides, so it can be zeroed or taken off in service.
manifold.material: Forged stainless steel body, valve stems and seats

process_flange.name: Process flange
process_flange.does: Brings the process pressure through two ports to the sensor module's isolating diaphragms; PTFE O-rings seal it to the module.

drain_vents.name: Drain/vent valves
drain_vents.does: Screwed into the process flange beside each port: opened to drain liquid or vent gas trapped in the flange chambers.

sensor_module.name: Sensor module
sensor_module.does: Turns the process pressure into an electrical signal: the isolating diaphragms pass it through the fill fluid to the sensing cell.
sensor_module.sealed_why: The sensor module is sealed and filled at the factory and is replaced as a unit, never opened in the field.

isolator.name: Isolating diaphragms
isolator.does: Thin corrugated diaphragms that meet the process and pass its pressure to the fill fluid; never scratched, punctured or pressed.

sensor_cell.name: Sensing cell
sensor_cell.does: A capacitance cell: the fill fluid moves its sensing diaphragm between two plates, and the change in capacitance measures the pressure.
sensor_cell.material: Silicone fill fluid, metal and ceramic cell

housing.name: Electronics housing
housing.does: Threaded onto the sensor module's neck; a wall divides it into the electronics compartment and the field terminal compartment, each with its cover.

cover_front.name: Electronics cover
cover_front.does: Screws onto the electronics side of the housing, metal to metal; its window shows the display.
cover_front.sealed_why: The window is set in the cover at the factory: the cover and its window are one spare part.

window.name: Display window
window.does: The glass in the electronics cover through which the display is read.

cover_back.name: Terminal cover
cover_back.does: Screws onto the side marked "FIELD TERMINALS"; taken off to reach the wiring.

electronics.name: Electronics board
electronics.does: Linearises the sensor's signal and makes the 4–20 mA output and its HART signal; held in the housing by two captive screws.

display.name: LCD display
display.does: Shows the measured value; plugs onto the electronics board with a pin connector and can be turned in steps.

terminal_block.name: Terminal block
terminal_block.does: Where the loop wires land: the signal terminals and the test terminals; slides onto the housing's power posts, held by two screws.

cable_gland.name: Cable gland
cable_gland.does: Seals the loop cable where it enters the terminal compartment.

text: Set the sensor module on the bench, its isolating diaphragms down and clear of anything that could scratch them.
The isolating diaphragms come with the sensor module: never scratch, puncture or press them.
The sensing cell is sealed inside the sensor module with its fill fluid.
Tuck the ribbon cable into the internal black cap, lower the electronics housing onto the module and turn it clockwise until it is no more than one full turn from flush.
why: Turned with the cable caught, the housing would tear the ribbon cable.
needs: sensor_module
The housing threads onto the sensor module's neck: put the sensor module in place first.
Unscrew the housing before the sensor module is moved.

text: Tighten the housing rotation set screw.
needs: housing
The set screw locks the housing on the module: thread the housing on first.
Loosen the housing rotation set screw one full turn before unscrewing the housing.

text: Connect the ribbon cable to the electronics board, slide the board in by its two captive screws onto the power posts without forcing it, and tighten the screws.
why: The board is sensitive to static: hold it by its captive screws.
needs: housing
The electronics board goes into the housing: put the housing on first.
Take the electronics board out and unplug its ribbon cable before the housing comes off the module.

text: Plug the LCD display onto the board's pin connector, turned the way it is to be read.
needs: electronics
The display plugs onto the electronics board: fit the board first.
Take the display off before the electronics board comes out.

text: Screw the electronics cover on until it meets the housing metal to metal.
why: Covers engaged metal to metal seal the housing and keep it explosion-proof.
needs: electronics
Fit the electronics board before closing the electronics cover.
Take the electronics cover off before the electronics board.
display
Fit the display before closing the electronics cover.
Take the electronics cover off before the display.

text: The window comes with the electronics cover.
Slide the terminal block onto the housing's power posts and tighten its two captive screws.
Screw the cable gland into the conduit entry of the terminal compartment.
Screw the terminal cover on, fully engaged.
needs: terminal_block
Fit the terminal block before closing the terminal cover.
Take the terminal cover off before the terminal block.

text: Check the PTFE O-rings, then hold the process flange on the sensor module with its two alignment screws, finger tight.
why: Overtightened, the alignment screws would pull the flange out of line with the module.
needs: sensor_module
The process flange goes onto the sensor module's diaphragms: put the module in place first.
Take the process flange off before the sensor module is moved.

text: Fit the four flange bolts finger tight, then tighten them crosswise, first to the initial and then to the final torque.
needs: process_flange
The flange bolts go in once the process flange sits on the sensor module.
Take the four flange bolts out before the process flange comes off.

text: Wrap the drain/vent valves' threads with sealing tape and screw them into the flange, their openings pointing down.
Bolt the manifold under the process flange, as its maker's instructions say.
needs: process_flange
The manifold bolts under the process flange: fit the flange first.
Take the manifold off before the process flange.
